lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is working late. And I'm a bit tired today — I worked until midnight yesterday.
Why so late?
A big deadline. The report was due this morning, so I had to burn the midnight oil.
Did you get paid for the overtime?
[laugh] No. That's not how it works in my office.
My cousin Nigar is a nurse. She works night shifts — from eight in the evening to eight in the morning.
Twelve hours at night? How does she sleep?
With black curtains and earplugs. She sleeps when everyone else is awake.
That sounds really hard on the body.
It is. After a month of nights she was completely exhausted. She told me, "I can't run on empty any more."
In England many doctors and nurses leave because of burnout. It's a big problem.
Here too. Now she does nights only one week a month.
Good. My secret for long days is a nap. Twenty minutes after lunch, and I'm a new man.
In the office?
In my car! [chuckle] With the seat back.
My dad was a baker. He started at three in the morning, every day, for thirty years.
Three in the morning! When did he finish?
At noon. Then he said, "Okay, let's call it a day," and slept all afternoon.
Honestly, that sounds better than my office.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: do you ever work or study late — and how do you stay awake?
And when do you call it a day? See you next time!
Bye for now!
